summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted with shortness of breath and substernal chest pain, found to be due to acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbated by medication non-compliance and dietary indiscretion. She had stopped her furosemide weeks prior and gained approximately 10 pounds. Initial concern for pulmonary embolism was raised due to elevated D-dimer, but V/Q scan and lower extremity ultrasound were negative, and her iodine allergy precluded CT angiography. She was treated with IV furosemide, achieving a 4-liter net negative fluid balance, and was restarted on oral furosemide at discharge. She also had bilateral conjunctivitis treated with ciprofloxacin eye drops. Her platelet count, low due to immune thrombocytopenia, improved during admission. She was discharged home with services after clinical improvement, with instructions to monitor weight, complete outpatient labs, and follow up with her cardiologist regarding medication adjustments.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Diaphragmatic hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
Osteoarthrosis, localized, not specified whether primary or secondary, lower leg
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of breast
